messages:
sourav: Ran a short nsys capture to debug a latency spike during batching; saw kernel start times 'drift' across iterations and a big pause right after KV eviction :thinking_face:
elaine: can you paste the exact nsys command you used? curious about capture range and sampling settings
anna: short captures often miss tail kernels. if you used a tiny duration, osrt/scheduler markers might be truncated
sourav: used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx:112233-112240 -o run.qdrep --sample=none --duration=8s`
mike: ok two quick things: 1) `--sample=none` drops sampling counters (so you lose CPU stacks) 2) `--capture-range=nvtx` depends on NVTX brackets being consistent — if a bracket spans beyond the capture window you get partial events
elaine: try increasing duration to 20-30s and enable CPU sampling: `--sample=cpu --sample-frequency=1000` — that helped us surface the host thread queuing before kernels
sourav: re-ran with `--sample=cpu --duration=25s --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o wide.qdrep` and the pause aligns with a KV eviction GC job on host thread `kv-evictd` :boom:
anna: that's interesting. eviction runs can shift kernel selection heuristics if cache misses increase seq_len; runtime picks a larger kernel for packing and that causes the spike
mike: also inspect the OSRT timeline: OSRT scheduling marks will show when request batching window opened vs when a kernel actually launched — sometimes batching heuristics back off if runtime sees long tail latency
sourav: saw exact pattern: NVTX bracket for request A -> small kernels for a few iters -> eviction NVTX bracket -> next NVTX bracket has larger matmul kernel. looks like kernel selection swapped to a different kernel id after cache miss
ci-bot: automated note: captured `wide.qdrep` uploaded to `gs://redwood-perf/nsys/1977654321-wide.qdrep` for trace team review :white_check_mark:
elaine: for future captures, when debugging kernel selection also dump `RT_LOG=kernel_selector=debug` (or equivalent) so logs map kernels -> selected algo ids
anna: and add `--capture-range=nvtx:bracket_start-bracket_end` with explicit bracket ids from logs (not timestamps) to avoid off-by-one capture windows
mike: small tip — if the capture file gets huge, use `nsys stats` to extract timeline subset, or `nsys ui` to open and filter OSRT lanes
sourav: follow-up plan: 1) reproduce with 30s capture + cpu sampling, 2) collect kernel selector logs, 3) run a deterministic KV-evict stress to confirm causality. I'll post the new qdrep link when done :thumbsup:
anna: sounds good. ping me once you have the qdrep and the selector log, happy to dig into kernel ids and model seq_len distribution
anna: also consider toggling `--sample-frequency` down if file size is a concern (1000 -> 200) — still useful for hotspots
sourav: thanks folks — saving this capture workflow as a short checklist in the perf runbook after we confirm reproducible case :memo:
